name: Dulan's Soul Food Kitchen
tagline: Crenshaw's soul food institution, serving the neighborhood since 1985.
description: A Crenshaw District cornerstone where cafeteria-style trays are loaded with smothered chicken, oxtails, candied yams and cornbread. Dulan's has fed South LA for four decades and remains a first stop for anyone looking for the real thing.

name: Harold & Belle's
tagline: Family-run Creole fine dining in Jefferson Park since 1969.
description: Three generations of the Legaux family have run this Creole dining room, plating gumbo, étouffée and jambalaya in portions built for sharing. One of the oldest continuously Black-owned restaurants in Los Angeles.

name: Post & Beam
tagline: Modern California cooking rooted in the Black South, in Baldwin Hills.
description: A polished neighborhood restaurant in Baldwin Hills Crenshaw Plaza pairing seasonal California produce with Southern technique. The patio and bar have made it a standing meeting place for Black LA.

name: Alta Adams
tagline: West Adams dining room serving California soul food and natural wine.
description: Chef Keith Corbin's West Adams restaurant reads Southern cooking through California ingredients — collards, blackened catfish, cornbread — alongside a natural wine list and a courtyard that fills every night of the week.

name: Hotville Chicken
tagline: Nashville hot chicken from the family that helped invent it.
description: Kim Prince carries her family's Nashville hot chicken lineage west, frying to a heat scale that runs from mild to genuinely punishing. Sides, sweet tea and a Baldwin Hills counter that stays busy.

name: Earle's on Crenshaw
tagline: Crenshaw hot dog stand turned neighborhood landmark.
description: The Earle brothers started with a cart on Crenshaw and built it into a counter known for loaded dogs, vegan links and gumbo. A South LA staple that has outlasted most of the block.

name: Ackee Bamboo Jamaican Cuisine
tagline: Family-run Jamaican kitchen in the heart of Leimert Park.
description: Jerk chicken, oxtail, curry goat and festival, cooked by the Bonner family and served to a Leimert Park crowd that treats the dining room as an extension of the village. Long a fixture of the Degnan Boulevard corridor.

name: Sky's Gourmet Tacos
tagline: Soul-food seasoning meets the taco, on Pico since 1992.
description: Barbara Burrell built a following on tacos that run through a Black Angeleno palate — shrimp, catfish, garlic-heavy salsas. A Pico-Fairfax original that has been imitated across the city.

name: Simply Wholesome
tagline: Health food kitchen and juice bar on Slauson since 1984.
description: Part restaurant, part supplement shop, Simply Wholesome has served the Windsor Hills and View Park communities vegetarian patties, smoothies and herbal remedies for four decades. A rare wellness anchor built inside a Black neighborhood.

name: Hilltop Coffee + Kitchen
tagline: Coffee shop built as a gathering place for South LA.
description: Founded with actor Yvonne Orji among its backers, Hilltop was designed as the third place South LA had been missing — good espresso, a full kitchen, and enough table space that people actually stay. Locations in View Park, Inglewood and Eagle Rock.

name: Sip & Sonder
tagline: Inglewood coffee house, roastery and creative workspace.
description: Two former attorneys built Sip & Sonder into Inglewood's coffee anchor — a roastery, a café and a working room for the neighborhood's creatives. Programming and residencies run alongside the espresso bar.

name: Delicious Pizza
tagline: West Adams pizzeria wired into LA's hip-hop history.
description: Built inside the old Delicious Vinyl orbit, this West Adams pizzeria pairs thin-crust pies with a record-shop sensibility — murals, a sound system that matters, and a room that fills with the neighborhood after work.

name: Honey's Kettle Fried Chicken
tagline: Kettle-fried chicken and honey biscuits in Culver City.
description: Vincent Williams fries to order in open kettles, which is why the line moves slowly and nobody minds. Chicken, biscuits, honey on the table, and a Culver City dining room that has been packed for years.

name: Southern Girl Desserts
tagline: Cupcakes, cobblers and layer cakes in Baldwin Hills.
description: A Baldwin Hills bakery known for red velvet, sweet potato pie and cobbler by the pan. Southern Girl has been the default order for South LA birthdays, repasts and Sunday dinners for over a decade.
address_line_1: 3650 W Martin Luther King Jr Blvd

name: Stuff I Eat
tagline: Chef Babette's plant-based kitchen in downtown Inglewood.
description: Babette Davis has been serving raw and cooked vegan food in Inglewood since well before it was fashionable — bowls, wraps, and a nacho plate that converts skeptics. A wellness landmark for Black LA.

name: Bloom & Plume Coffee
tagline: Maximalist coffee bar from florist Maurice Harris.
description: Maurice Harris took the visual language of his floral studio and built a coffee bar out of it — saturated color, house syrups, and drinks named with a sense of humor. A Historic Filipinotown corner that photographs as well as it pours.

name: Phillips Barbecue
tagline: Pit-smoked ribs and hot links, an LA barbecue institution.
description: Phillips has been the answer to "where's the barbecue" in Black Los Angeles for decades — tips, links, ribs, and a sauce people buy by the jar. Order at the window, eat in the car, no apologies.

name: Hawkins House of Burgers
tagline: Watts burger stand serving oversized plates since 1939.
description: Cynthia Hawkins runs a Watts institution founded by her family, known for burgers stacked past reason and a community role that goes well past food. One of the oldest Black-owned restaurants in Los Angeles.

name: Mel's Fish Shack
tagline: Fried catfish and red snapper, Leimert Park style.
description: A no-frills fish shack on Marlton frying catfish, snapper and shrimp to order with hot sauce on the side. The kind of place that has never needed to advertise.

name: Woody's Bar-B-Que
tagline: Slauson Avenue barbecue counter, a South LA constant.
description: Ribs, links, chicken and sides sold over a counter on Slauson. Woody's has been part of the Hyde Park routine for decades, and the sauce is the reason.

name: Fixins Soul Kitchen
tagline: Downtown LA soul food from former mayor Kevin Johnson.
description: A full-service soul food dining room downtown — fried chicken, catfish, mac and cheese, and a bar — built to put Black cooking on a South Park block that had none.

name: Vicky's All Day
tagline: West Adams all-day café named for a neighborhood elder.
description: A West Adams corner café serving breakfast into the evening, named in tribute to a longtime neighbor. Coffee, sandwiches, and a patio that functions as the block's living room.

name: All Flavor No Grease
tagline: LA's most-followed taco truck, built on social media and long lines.
description: A roving taco operation that turned an Instagram following into some of the longest lines in the city. Locations change; the asada does not.

name: Trap Kitchen LA
tagline: Two friends from rival neighborhoods turned catering into a movement.
description: Malachi Jenkins and Roberto Smith built Trap Kitchen out of a Compton apartment into a catering and pop-up brand with national reach — pineapple bowls, lobster mac, and a story about what cooperation across sets can look like.

name: Bridgetown Roti
tagline: Caribbean roti and doubles from chef Rashida Holmes.
description: Rashida Holmes cooks the Barbadian and Trinidadian food she grew up on — roti, doubles, pepper sauce — with a chef's precision. Started as a pop-up, now one of LA's most talked-about Caribbean kitchens.

name: The World Stage
tagline: Leimert Park's jazz and poetry workshop, founded by Billy Higgins.
description: Drummer Billy Higgins and poet Kamau Daáood opened The World Stage in 1989 as a performance and education space. Jazz jams, writers' workshops and drum circles have run continuously since, making it the cultural anchor of Degnan Boulevard.

name: Barbara Morrison Performing Arts Center
tagline: Leimert Park venue built by the late jazz vocalist Barbara Morrison.
description: A small Leimert Park theater founded by vocalist Barbara Morrison for live music, youth programs and community performance. It remains a working stage for LA's jazz and blues players.

name: Band of Vices
tagline: West Adams contemporary art gallery centering artists of color.
description: Terrell Tilford's West Adams gallery shows contemporary work with a deliberate focus on Black and brown artists, running a program that has moved several careers from local to national.

name: Museum of African American Art
tagline: Founded by Dr. Samella Lewis, tucked inside Baldwin Hills Crenshaw Plaza.
description: Artist and historian Dr. Samella Lewis founded MAAA in 1976 to collect and show African American art at a time when few institutions would. Free admission, third floor of the mall, a permanent Palmer Hayden collection.

name: Art + Practice
tagline: Leimert Park art and social services campus founded by Mark Bradford.
description: Artist Mark Bradford, Allan DiCastro and Eileen Harris Norton built Art + Practice as a hybrid — free contemporary art exhibitions alongside services for foster youth, on the same Leimert Park block.

name: KAOS Network
tagline: Leimert Park media arts lab and home of Project Blowed.
description: Ben Caldwell's media arts center has trained generations of Leimert Park kids in video, animation and digital art, and hosts Project Blowed — the longest-running open mic in hip-hop.

name: Malik Books
tagline: Family-owned bookstore centering Black authors, in Baldwin Hills.
description: Malik and April Muhammad have run this bookstore since 1990, stocking Black literature, history and children's titles that chain stores skip. A Baldwin Hills Crenshaw Plaza fixture with a second location in Culver City.
address_line_1: 3650 W Martin Luther King Jr Blvd

name: Reparations Club
tagline: Concept shop and bookstore curated by and for the culture.
description: Jazzi McGilbert's West Adams shop is part bookstore, part gallery, part gathering room — a tightly curated selection of books, zines and goods with a programming calendar that draws the city's creative class.

name: The Salt Eaters Bookshop
tagline: Inglewood bookstore devoted to Black women, femmes and queer writers.
description: Asha Grant named the shop for Toni Cade Bambara's novel and built the inventory around Black women, femme and queer authors. Reading groups and author events run out of the Inglewood storefront.

name: Sole Folks
tagline: Leimert Park retail incubator for independent Black designers.
description: Part storefront, part accelerator — Sole Folks gives emerging Black designers and brands a Leimert Park retail floor, plus the business support to actually use it.

name: The Marathon Clothing
tagline: Nipsey Hussle's Crenshaw store and the corner it made famous.
description: The smart store Nipsey Hussle opened at Slauson and Crenshaw, and the site of the memorial that followed. Apparel, and a pilgrimage point for people who understood what he was building.

name: Nappily Naturals & Apothecary
tagline: Leimert Park herb shop and natural hair care apothecary.
description: Bulk herbs, teas, oils and natural hair products on Degnan Boulevard, with staff who will actually talk you through what you're buying. A Leimert Park wellness anchor.

name: Sika
tagline: African art, textiles and imports on Degnan Boulevard.
description: One of Leimert Park's longest-standing shops, selling African masks, fabric, jewelry and imports. The kind of inventory you cannot get online without losing the conversation that comes with it.

name: Hoorae Media
tagline: Issa Rae's Los Angeles media company.
description: The production and media company Issa Rae built after Insecure, spanning film, television, music and digital. Headquartered in LA with a deliberate practice of hiring and developing Black talent behind the camera.

name: Slauson & Co.
tagline: Early-stage venture firm investing in overlooked founders.
description: Austin Clements and Ajay Relan built Slauson & Co. to put early capital into founders that traditional venture routinely passes on, with a practice grounded in South LA rather than Sand Hill Road.
